data.description:
`c11 launch-agent` resolves the child's working directory from the LAUNCHING SURFACE's cwd.
In a worktree fleet that means the default behaviour is to drop a new agent into whatever
worktree its parent happens to be working in — i.e. another agent's ACTIVE, dirty branch.

HIT FOR REAL, 2026-08-05 (Acetate). An orchestrator working in
`acetate-worktrees/lyrics-accuracy` (branch `fix/ACE-791-whisper-tuning`, uncommitted
changes present) launched three Codex implementers. All three started INSIDE that worktree.
Two had their briefs swallowed by a Codex version-update prompt and were left sitting at a
bare shell in the parent's tree. Nothing was damaged — one agent only read files, and the
parent committed its outstanding work before re-briefing — but any edit would have collided
with an in-flight lane, and the collision would have been attributed to the wrong agent.

WHY IT IS WORTH A GUARD RATHER THAN JUST A BETTER DEFAULT: the failure is SILENT. The child
gets a perfectly working shell in a directory it has no way of knowing is contested. It has
no signal, the parent has no signal, and the damage surfaces later as unexplained changes in
someone else's branch — the most expensive shape of bug to trace. A default expresses a
preference; a guard enforces the invariant the fleet actually depends on, which is NOT
"children start at the project root" but "NO TWO AGENTS MUTATE THE SAME TREE". It also holds
when someone passes `--cwd` explicitly, which a default cannot.

DETECTION IS ONE COMPARISON — a linked worktree has a `.git` FILE, not a directory:

    git rev-parse --git-dir         # .../acetate/.git/worktrees/lyrics-accuracy
    git rev-parse --git-common-dir  # .../acetate/.git

They differ if and only if the cwd is a LINKED worktree (they are equal in the main
checkout). Verified on this machine.

PROPOSED BEHAVIOUR: when the resolved cwd is a linked worktree, refuse — or warn very
loudly — and name the branch so the message is actionable:

    cwd is a linked git worktree on 'fix/ACE-791-whisper-tuning' — this is likely another
    agent's active tree. Pass --cwd explicitly to override.

An explicit `--cwd` pointing at a linked worktree should still be ALLOWED (spawning a helper
into your own worktree is legitimate) but should say so once, so it is a choice rather than
an accident. Only the INHERITED case should be refused outright.

RELATED: the sibling ticket on defaulting to the workspace directory. These are complements,
not alternatives — the default decides where agents usually land, the guard decides what can
never happen quietly.
data.title: launch-agent: refuse to start an agent in another agent's linked worktree

data.body:
Trident plan review complete (9 agents × 3 lenses, pack: notes/trident-review-C11-193-plan-pack-20260806-1200/, action contract attached as art_01KZBZXVRDHEP9G6TJB0Z4BWH1).

VERDICT: revise-then-proceed — 8/9 reviewers judged the plan not implementable as written; the guard thesis itself (refuse inherited, permit explicit) was unanimously endorsed.

APPLIED to plan rev 2 (all verified against the working tree by the synthesis pass):
- B1: reuse GitContextResolver instead of authoring a second --git-dir/--git-common-dir probe (5 reviewers).
- B2: introduce a provenance-carrying effective-cwd value; today the inherited cwd is nil at the named seam and materializes downstream, so there is nothing to probe; probed path must equal spawned path (6 reviewers).
- B3: agent.launch is main-actor routed while GitContextResolver.resolve traps on main — added explicit off-main threading step (6 reviewers).
- B4: named error code inherited_linked_worktree + error.data schema; the promised acknowledgement was invisible in human mode because printV2Payload discards the warnings array outside --json — now stderr + JSON (6 reviewers).
- B5: decision table for degraded git states, fail-open-with-warning default on indeterminate inherited probe, latency budget, refusal strictly pre-mutation (6 reviewers).
- B6: C11-194 lands first and owns the shared resolver; cross-ticket matrix cases named (all 9 reviewers — strongest consensus in the pack).
- I1–I5, M1–M2: docs+skill deliverable w/ sync-installed-skills (CLAUDE.md hard rule), entry-point scope declared, tests extended to prove the refusal not just the predicate, wire-level definition of explicit, detached-HEAD message contract, test-target membership named, honest tripwire framing.
- Step 10 rewritten to defer xcodebuild to CI per the standing C11-181 operator instruction (resolves reviewer disagreement S3 in favor of the recorded rule).

SKIPPED (evolutionary, do not fold into a guard ticket — recorded for the roadmap): E1 stamp git tree/branch as surface metadata at birth; E2 ship warn-and-count before flipping to refuse; E3 --worktree new auto-provisioning. See synthesis-evolutionary.md.

FILED SEPARATELY: C11-195 — project .c11/agents.json lookup uses the app process cwd on the default launch path (latent bug found during review, verified).

REVIEWER MISREADS excluded from triage: adversarial-gemini's claim that the CLI forwards $PWD as --cwd (false — cwd param only sent when --cwd given); standard-gemini's ready-to-execute headline (contradicted by its own body).

OPEN PRODUCT CALLS → needs-human (see plan's final section): S1 workspace-root explicitness, S2 house-workflow false positives (three non-converging remedies; option b changes the guard's shape and would need re-review), S4 what the guard delivers if --cwd passes.

data.reason: Trident verdict: revise-then-proceed. Plan rev 2 applied (13 validated findings absorbed; see comment + attached synthesis-action). Three product calls gate implementation past step 1: (1) S1 — does a C11-194 workspace root count as explicit intent or inherited default when it is a linked worktree? (2) S2 — the guard as specified refuses the house lattice-orchestrator shape (delegator launching helpers from its own worktree; 38 linked worktrees live here). Pick a remedy: --allow-worktree/--force flag, live-surface-occupancy rule instead of the linked-worktree proxy (changes guard shape, needs re-review), or warn-and-count first. (3) S4 — confirm the visibility-over-enforcement trade of permitting explicit --cwd, or choose a harder override. Also: consensus is C11-194 lands first and owns the shared cwd resolver — confirm sequencing.

data.note: The operator's implementation brief resolves all three calls: workspace roots are inherited and guarded, explicit --cwd is the warned override, and C11-193 then C11-194 ship together on one branch.

data.body:
Operator call 2026-08-06 on the Trident S1/S2/S4 product questions: WARN, DO NOT REFUSE.

The guard emits a named warning carrying the offending worktree path and the launch proceeds. Rationale: the house lattice-orchestrator workflow deliberately runs one delegator per linked worktree and this checkout has 38 live, so a hard refusal would break the normal way of working. A stranded delegator fleet is a worse failure than a missed warning.

Binding on the rework:
- The warning must reach BOTH stderr and the --json output. The review found the CLI discards the warnings array outside --json; an invisible acknowledgement is not an acknowledgement.
- The warning carries a named error code, not just prose.
- Explicit --cwd stays permitted.
- A C11-194 workspace root counts as explicit intent.
- C11-194 lands first and owns the shared resolver, per the ordering all nine reviewers flagged.

(Note: the needs_human flag was not set on this ticket when I got here, so this comment is the record. PR #407's CI is red on 'Set up job' — runner infrastructure, not code.)

Plan updated to rev 3, folding the operator ruling (ev_01KZC3P8G4CCVP6Y3A56WADTJ5) into the build contract: guard outcome is now .allow / .allowWithWarning only — no .reject. linked_worktree_cwd becomes a warning code carried in both stderr and the JSON warnings array; .workspaceRoot origin classifies as explicit intent; degraded probe states fail open; test steps 8b/8e now assert the launch PROCEEDS with exactly one warning rather than asserting refusal. Rework note for PR #407: convert the d7c21ef4c rejection path (exit 1 on inherited) to the non-blocking warning while keeping the detection, provenance, and threading work.

provenance.reason: Operator superseded refusal with coded warning-and-proceed; C11-194 resolver remains first.
